$schema: durable Tartaria mechanics cartography — human-reachability model
generatedNote: Phase 5A, Part 3. Seeded from 8 parallel research passes tracing 40 owner-specified targets (some split into multiple state-sensitive rows, some merged where genuinely the same door). Hand-maintained from here on — do not regenerate wholesale.

reachabilityClasses.PLAYER_UI_REACHABLE: Invocable through a production UI control visible to a human when its production gate is satisfied.
reachabilityClasses.PLAYER_COMMAND_REACHABLE: Invocable through the production typed-command/parser surface when its production gate is satisfied.
reachabilityClasses.PLAYER_DERIVABLE: Not directly presented as a button/command but legitimately derivable by a capable human from player-visible information (includes purely automatic resolutions the player can observe and anticipate).
reachabilityClasses.STORE_ONLY: A store/internal action exists but no legitimate player-facing UI or command reaches it in the relevant state.
reachabilityClasses.TELEMETRY_ONLY: Available to instrumentation but not to the player.
reachabilityClasses.HIDDEN_FUTURE: Hidden information, future state, undisclosed RNG result, or other knowledge unavailable to a player at decision time.
reachabilityClasses.UNRESOLVED: Current evidence is insufficient to classify honestly.

playerLegitimateStandard: For canonical Walker purposes, an action is player-legitimate only when: (1) the human can perceive enough information to choose it; (2) the production game exposes the action in that state; (3) the harness respects the same production gate; (4) the harness does not bypass the player surface to obtain a capability unavailable through that surface. A direct store invocation is NOT automatically illegitimate — it is an acceptable harness implementation for a UI-only button when the production UI exposes that exact action, the harness independently enforces the same visible gate, no hidden state unavailable to the player is used, and the direct call produces the same production mechanism.

rows.name: Continue travel — no live enemies
rows.statePrecondition: currentScene.enemies.length === 0
rows.productionSource: app/state/gameStore.ts:26536 (continueTravel); app/components/InputBox.tsx:821,904

rows.name: Continue travel — live enemies present
rows.statePrecondition: currentScene.enemies.length > 0 (inCombat=true)
rows.productionSource: app/state/gameStore.ts:26536-26687 continueTravel() (no enemy gate anywhere in the function); app/components/InputBox.tsx:821 (`{!inCombat && (...travel row...)}`); app/screens/ExplorationScreen.tsx:1452 (inCombat derivation)
rows.playerVisibleGate: None reachable — the entire travel row is unmounted while enemies are present, and no typed command routes to continueTravel() either (typed "continue" is redirected into combat, gameStore.ts:17892-17898).
rows.harnessLocation: test-utils/canonical/actionExecutor.ts:172 travelContinue() — calls the store method directly, bypassing the UI, which is how this gap was proven
rows.rationale: continueTravel() itself has no enemy gate at the store layer; production never reaches it in this state through any player-facing surface. This is the founding STORE_ONLY case for the whole reachability model.
rows.notes: Root cause of the invalidated Phase 3D Asgardar journey — see evidenceCorrections.json#EC-007/EC-008.

rows.name: Attack
rows.statePrecondition: Live activeEnemy in-range (targetBand not null).
rows.productionSource: app/state/gameStore.ts:14216 case 'attack'; app/components/InputBox.tsx:1040/1059/1066 (weapon QuickBtns)
rows.playerVisibleGate: Requires a live, in-range enemy; no cooldown.
rows.rationale: submitPlayerAction('attack') is the exact door both weapon QuickBtns and the harness call.

rows.name: Flee
rows.statePrecondition: Live enemies present; FLEE chip always rendered while inCombat (elevated/climbing state dives to base instead).
rows.productionSource: app/components/InputBox.tsx:1157 (flee chip, live odds via fleeOddsFor); app/engine/parser.ts:62-68 (escape intent: flee/run/escape/bolt/scram); app/state/gameStore.ts:16672,22639,23043 (case 'escape'); app/engine/combatRules.ts:906-939 (contested pursuit)
rows.playerVisibleGate: Not HP-gated, not enemy-type-gated; hidden only while a roll card is open (pendingRolls).
rows.rationale: Contested roll (player d20+DEX vs. fastest live pursuer's d20+speed, flat DC 9 with no pursuer). SUCCESS clears currentScene.enemies entirely and lets travel resume normally; FLEE_STAMINA_COST(3) is charged after the fact, never as a gate (can flee at 0 stamina). FAILURE: no state change, every living enemy gets a free attack-of-opportunity, turn wasted, fleeAttempts increments (raises future difficulty on unscripted lineups). The harness combatFlee() resolves through the identical fleePursuitFor/pendingRolls machinery — no shortcut.
rows.notes: Mechanically legitimate; whether it is sufficient to solve fresh-character survivability is explicitly NOT decided here — see I-037.

rows.name: Dodge
rows.statePrecondition: Not elevated/climbing; dodge cooldown ready (dodgeCooldown.dodgeReady); not already dodging.
rows.productionSource: app/components/InputBox.tsx:1131 (cooldownFill=dodgeFill); app/state/gameStore.ts:18242-18337 case 'dodge'; app/state/combatResolution.ts:2132-2306 (opposed resolution)
rows.playerVisibleGate: Cooldown (tier-scaled), unavailable while elevated, already-dodging guard.
rows.rationale: Sets a single-shot 'dodging' status resolved via an opposed d20+DEX-vs-attacker roll on the NEXT incoming attack (applyEnemyCounter) — not a passive AC bonus. Harness calls the identical door.

rows.name: Block
rows.statePrecondition: Off-hand item passes itemIsShield (offShieldName truthy); not elevated.
rows.productionSource: app/components/InputBox.tsx:1138; app/state/gameStore.ts:18339-18389 case 'block'; app/state/combatResolution.ts:1878-1902 (shield_block absorption)
rows.playerVisibleGate: Genuinely shield-gated — no equipped off-hand shield refuses with an explicit line naming DODGE as the fallback.
rows.rationale: Single-shot 'shield_block' status guarantees full absorption of the first incoming blow (no roll); harness calls the same door with no shield-check bypass.

rows.name: Combat healing use — "✚ heals" quick-bar chip (useHealBatch)
rows.statePrecondition: Mid-fight, live enemies present; medkitItems.length>0.
rows.productionSource: app/components/InputBox.tsx:1428-1493 (medkit picker) -> app/state/slices/inventorySlice.ts:526 useHealBatch

rows.harnessLocation: none exists — no actionExecutor.ts method calls useHealBatch
rows.rationale: This is the reliable, always-available production door a real player actually uses to heal mid-combat, built specifically to dodge the pendingRolls dead-button bug on the generic "use" path (see combat-consumable-use-generic, the sibling row). The canonical harness has no method for it at all — a genuine reachability gap, not merely a qualification-evidence gap.

rows.name: Combat consumable/healing use — generic "use <item>"
rows.statePrecondition: Mid-fight, live enemies present; item owned.
rows.productionSource: app/state/gameStore.ts:17069-17130 case 'rest' (item branch, combatHealNoCounter); app/state/gameStore.ts:16674-16763 case 'use_relic' (generic 'use X')

rows.rationale: A real, legitimate production door, and the harness faithfully mirrors it — but production itself documents this specific path as unreliable mid-fight (OTA-1658), which the sibling heals-chip door was built to route around. Reachable, just not the door a player would actually rely on in combat.

rows.name: Death/resurrection choice (resurrectSlot -> spendGemAndRevive)
rows.statePrecondition: player.dead===true; DeathOverlay auto-dismisses to currentScreen:'title', player:null.
rows.productionSource: app/state/slices/slotSlice.ts:713-779 resurrectSlot() (calls saveSystem.ts:591 spendGemAndRevive); wired at app/screens/TitleScreen.tsx:295,1574
rows.playerVisibleGate: Title-screen roster shows a DEAD badge and, if resurrectionGems>0, a gem-count badge plus a "RESURRECT THIS TARTARIAN" band. Tapping opens a confirm modal: with gems, a Resurrect button calling resurrectSlot(slotId); with zero gems, an informational modal only (OK button, no revive path). After death itself, DeathOverlay is a non-interactive lore crawl with no revive option inside the death flow — the resurrection door lives one screen removed, at the title-screen roster.
rows.rationale: Real, player-tappable store action with an explicit gem-count>0 UI gate and no free-text equivalent; unexercised by the canonical harness despite being fully reachable. PlayerView (test-utils/canonical/playerView.ts) does not currently expose resurrectionGems/resurrectedFromDeathId at all, so policy cannot act on this even if a harness method existed.

rows.name: Nexus/ending choice (seal/unleash/preserve/stay)
rows.statePrecondition: mainQuest.phase==='choice' (reached automatically when locationId==='mud_flood_nexus' via ordinary travel arrival, which fires triggerMainQuest({kind:'reached_nexus'}) advancing 'descent'->'choice'; per source comment this requires all 9 Cores already present since it is documented as "Final").
rows.productionSource: app/state/gameStore.ts:7722-7723,30540 chooseEndingMainQuest(ending); reached_nexus trigger at gameStore.ts:24681; UI: app/screens/ContractsScreen.tsx:1017,1027,1037,1052 (four buttons, one per ending)
rows.playerVisibleGate: Reaching the Nexus location is an ordinary, player-visible travel arrival (no hidden trigger). The four ending buttons (seal/unleash/preserve/stay) are directly visible on ContractsScreen once phase='choice'; no typed-command path found for choosing an ending.
rows.harnessLocation: test-utils/canonical/actionExecutor.ts:456-465 nexusArrive() — unconditionally throws "must never be CALLED outside P7"
rows.rationale: The production door and its UI are both real and player-reachable (confirmed this pass — resolves the prior UNRESOLVED status from the initial research pass); the harness deliberately stubs it out as an intentional P7-only boundary, not a reachability gap. Resolution POLICY (which ending to choose) remains a separate, unmade owner decision.

rows.name: Guardian summon/admission
rows.statePrecondition: Player stationed at an unrecovered Lost Capital, mainQuest.phase in revelation/cores, no live hostiles, coreSettleState pacing satisfied (bypassed for the player's first Guardian).
rows.productionSource: app/state/gameStore.ts:30578-30742 summonCoreGuardian()
rows.playerVisibleGate: Two UI surfaces call summonCoreGuardian() directly: ExplorationScreen.tsx ★ SUMMON chip (~2021-2038) and ContractsScreen.tsx ★ SUMMON chip (~890-904). Both stay pressable-but-refusing during a hostile-block or settle-wait, printing the exact in-world reason on tap, with the label switching among "★ SUMMON"/"★ FIGHT FIRST"/"★ SETTLING · Nh" — player-visible before attempting, not refusal-only discovery. No parser/typed command path found.
rows.rationale: Button labels derive from the same coreSettleState/summonHostiles helpers the action itself calls, so the chip cannot show "ready" while the action would refuse.

rows.name: Guardian combat entry
rows.statePrecondition: Guardian spawned into currentScene.enemies via summonCoreGuardian().
rows.productionSource: app/state/gameStore.ts submitPlayerAction attack/dodge/block/flee cases; flee-vs-Guardian special-case ~22704-22736
rows.playerVisibleGate: Same attack/dodge/block/flee UI and parser commands as any other enemy — no forced engagement, no UI lockout. Guardian-specific: knockout never applies (isSubduable requires enemyType==='human', all Guardians are aether_construct/mud_revenant — must be defeated outright); flee is allowed and contested but on success fully de-spawns and restores the Guardian on the next summon attempt (cannot be chipped down across visits, though damage the PLAYER took is kept).
rows.rationale: Uses the identical pendingRolls combat machinery as any encounter; the only Guardian-specific wrinkles (knockout-ineligibility, flee-resets-Guardian) are player-observable outcomes, not hidden gates.

rows.name: Core acquisition/resolution
rows.statePrecondition: Guardian enemy HP reaches 0 during normal combat resolution.
rows.productionSource: app/state/gameStore.ts:25467-25489 (resolveEnemyDefeat block) -> triggerMainQuest(kind:'core_recovered') at :25489; app/engine/mainQuest.ts:1073
rows.playerVisibleGate: None — no separate prompt/choice. Core grant, guardiansDefeated bookkeeping, and the mq_core_recovered milestone log all fire in the same synchronous block as the kill resolution, purely as a consequence of winning the fight.
rows.harnessLocation: none exists (correctly) — actionExecutor.ts:414-419 documents Core resolution as automatic, "observed via telemetry, never computed here"
rows.rationale: Pure resolution consequence of Guardian defeat, not a player action; classifying it as UI/COMMAND reachable would misrepresent the mechanic.

negativeEdges.statement: LIVE ENEMIES PRESENT does not expose CONTINUE TRAVEL to the player.
negativeEdges.evidence: InputBox.tsx:821 unmounts the entire travel row whenever currentScene.enemies.length>0; no typed command routes to continueTravel() in that state either.

negativeEdges.statement: A store/internal method existing does not imply a player action exists.
negativeEdges.evidence: Demonstrated repeatedly: continueTravel() (enemies present), Core acquisition (automatic resolution), applyCoatingToArmor (no executor, though genuinely UI-reachable — a harness gap, not a player-reachability gap).

negativeEdges.statement: A production UI door existing does not imply the canonical harness can exercise it.
negativeEdges.evidence: Bulk sell (3 UI paths), bulk repair, golem/dog combat participation, golem summon/arm, dog revive, death/resurrection — all PLAYER_UI_REACHABLE or PLAYER_COMMAND_REACHABLE in production with NO harness method at all.
